Commentary.Commentary: We are back for India's reply! The players are already out in the middle. Rohit Sharma and Shubman Gill are the two openers for India. There are 10 overs left on Day 2 and Mitchell Starc has the new ball in hand and is raring to go.
... SECOND INNINGS ...

For the first time in this series the Indian bowlers were absolutely pushed to their limits. The wicket does not have much help for the bowlers and it was a tough challenge for them. However, when the going gets tough, Ravichandran Ashwin steps up for his team and he did exactly that with an excellent six-wicket haul to give some hopes to the hosts. Mohammad Shami was brilliant as well with his spells and gave his all and picked up two crucial wickets. Axar Patel and Ravindra Jadeja chipped in with one each as well. However, now the Indian batters have their task cut out to get near this total. Join us in a bit for India's reply.

Australia learnt from their mistakes and in this game they were able to build a few good partnerships in the middle. The star of the show for them was Usman Khawaja with his brilliant hundred and he finished on 180 runs off 422 balls. Cameron Green also supported him well with his maiden Test hundred. Both of them added 208 runs together which took them near the 400-run mark, but some good contribution from Todd Murphy and Nathan Lyon got them to 480 runs which should give them a lot of confidence when they come out to bowl.

A massive batting effort from Australia! They have managed to score 480 runs in their first innings and this was by far their best batting performance in this series. India would have liked to restrict them to lower total than this, but this wicket is still good to bat on and they will back themselves to put up a good show.

OUT! TAKEN! Ravichandran Ashwin picks up his sixth wicket of the innings and Australia have been finally bundled out. Nicely flighted on a length and around off stump, Nathan Lyon puts a big stride forward as he looks to block. Lyon though doesn't get to the pitch of the ball and the outside edge is found. The ball flicks the keeper's legs and loops up kindly to Virat Kohli at first slip and he makes no mistake. Lyon's solid resistance comes to an end and Australia finish with 480 runs on the board.
Commentary.Howout: c Virat Kohli b Ravichandran Ashwin

We are back for the third session! The players are out in the middle now. Usman Khawaja and Nathan Lyon have the responsibilty to take Australia to an even more big total while India will be looking to bowl them out. Axar Patel has the ball in his hand. Also, Rohit Sharma has not come out to field and Cheteshwar Pujara is the stand-by skipper for India for now.
... DAY 2, SESSION 3 ...

Usman Khawaja and Cameron Green started from where they left off in the first session. Green did not take much time and registered his maiden Test hundred. However, he soon fell into Ashwin's trap and got out. After that, Ravichandran Ashwin showed his class and quickly picked a couple of wickets more to expose the lower order of Australia. The only thing for Australia is that Khawaja is still going and frustrating their bowlers, as well as the fact that the visitors have gone past the 400-run mark. Australia will look to get somewhere around 450 runs, while the hosts will hope to quickly wrap up the Australian innings when they come out in the last session. Join us at 2.30 pm IST (9 am GMT) to catch all the action in the third session.

Right then, 347 runs on the board already and a score of 450 or even 500 doesn't seem far-fetched given the nature of the surface. Australia will look to bat out another whole session without losing a wicket or two and post a big first inning total. India will look to come out with a bit more intent and make the Aussie batters play a few more shots. Will the fortunes change in the post-Lunch session? Join us at 12.10 pm IST (6.40 am GMT) to find out.

India have had a tough time out in the middle early on Day 2 as they haven't been able to create a single real wicket-taking opportunity. There was one outside edge early in the session which landed well short and one in the final over before Lunch as well but that was it. Mohammad Shami and Axar Patel bowled a fine spell at the start of the day but the others couldn't keep the pressure on the Aussie batters. Umesh Yadav had a torrid time with the second new ball last evening and once again he was targeted by the Aussies. There is hardly any spin available and it will certainly be a test of India's patience now.

Australia came into Day 2 on the back of a fine final session on Day 1 that saw both Usman Khawaja and Cameron Green score freely against the second new ball. The pair though stayed watchful in the first hour of Day 2 but did manage to score much more freely in the second hour with both batters taking a liking to Umesh Yadav. Khawaja who had already surpassed the 100-run mark went on to score over 150 runs and is still going strong. Green has been brilliant and is nearing a ton as well. The pair will like to take the visitors above the 400-run mark without getting out and build on from there.

PITCH REPORT - Murali Kartik is pitchside and he is joined by Dinesh Karthik. The latter says that run-scoring will get a little difficult, the ball won't turn much but the wicket will get slower. Adds that the odd delivery might straighten enough for the spinners but the pitch doesn't have many demons on it. Murali Kartik ends by saying that Day 2 will be a hard battle for the batters.

India, on the other hand, struggled a bit, as their spin trio was not as effective as it was in previous games. However, Mohammad Shami bowled really well on this tough wicket and picked up two crucial wickets, and he will look to get some early breakthroughs on Day 2 to quickly wrap up the Australian innings. Stay tuned for all the action, which starts in a bit.

Australia put on their best batting display in this series on Day 1, avoiding any kind of collapses. Usman Khawaja was the star of the show with his class hundred, and he will come out to bat along with Cameron Green to take them to a huge first innings total.

Hello and welcome to our coverage of Day 2 of this fourth and final Test between India and Australia. The Aussies are in a good position, and they will want to strengthen that, while India will hope to make some early inroads and comeback into this game.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1...

Right then, finally a day of test cricket on this tour where we didn't see the ball doing all sorts of things and this makes the final Test very interesting. Australia will now target the 350-run mark and set the tone for the rest of the game whereas India will look to pick up early wickets on Day 2 and keep the score as close to 300 as possible. It will be interesting to see which side is able to make their mark on the second day. Day 2 will begin on Friday at 9.30 am IST (4 am GMT) but you can catch our build-up a lot earlier. Cheers!

Usman Khawaja, the man of the moment is down for a quick chat. Khawaja says a lot of emotions are running through him and it is his third tour to India and finally getting a hundred here feels really special. He adds that at the start of the day and in the later stage of the day, they did not talk about anything and he just kept giving the strike to Travis Head early on and then to Cameron Green who was seeing the ball like a basketball. He also adds in his celebration that Green just wanted a hug as he wanted to congratulate him and they celebrated a bit emotionally. He also adds that he would like to thank all the coaches and those who supported him and helped him with the warm-ups that are best for him.

India will be a touch disappointed with that effort and even though the pitch wasn't anywhere near a raging turner, the overall intent with the ball was lacking. The hosts did extremely well to knock over Steven Smith and Peter Handscomb fairly early in the final session but couldn't go on and use that momentum in their favour. The bowlers bowled quite a few quiet overs but the wickets didn't come and once the second new ball was taken, runs started to flow quite thickly for the opposition and India ended the day on the back foot.

Australia came into the final session with just a couple of wickets down but the scoring rate was pretty low. Steven Smith got out early in the post-Tea session and he looked tentative to score runs. Peter Handscomb came out and played a few shots but was dismissed soon after. After that though, Usman Khawaja and Cameron Green remained watchful till the second new ball was taken. Green went into overdrive and punished the bowlers with Khawaja ticking along nicely as well and the latter ended with an unbeaten ton, the first by an Aussie batter on this tour.

A session that belongs to Australia as they have taken control of this game with a 77-run unbeaten partnership in 238 balls accumulating 74 runs in this session and not losing a single wicket which has happened for the first time in this series. Travis Head started off a bit tentatively but the dropped catch when he was on 7 woke him up and he started playing his strokes with much more intent which proved to be fruitful for the Aussies. He however played on shot too many and was eventually dismissed on a score of 32 looking to clear the infield. Marnus Labuschagne chopped one back onto his stumps but Usman Khawaja has looked at ease on this track. The Indian bowlers will have to be patient on this track as the pitch is not helping much so far. Will Australia continue to accumulate runs and build a strong first-inning score? Or will India claim a few more wickets after the break and grab the game by the scruff of the neck? We will find out what unfolds in the afternoon session shortly. Do join us at 12.10 pm IST (6.40 am GMT) for more action.

A shared session as the Aussies had the better start to the game putting on 75 runs on the board so far but India fought back well with a couple of crucial wickets to stake their claim in the game. Steven Smith will be happy with the way the openers started after winning the toss as the openers added 61 runs. Indian bowlers had their radar off to begin proceedings as they were all over the place and could not build any sort of rhythm. Srikar Bharat denied Umesh Yadav a wicket as he dropped an absolute sitter behind the wicket giving Travis Head a lifeline but wickets from Ravichandran Ashwin and Mohammad Shami along with some disciplined bowling in the last half an hour have brought the hosts back into contention.

We are done with the pre-match formalities and all set for the game to begin. The umpires make their way out to the center as the Indian players form a huddle near the boundary line and get some final instructions from their captain before dispersing to their respective fielding positions. Usman Khawaja and Travis Head will open the innings for Australia and will want to get off to a good start after winning the toss. Mohammad Shami has been handed the new ball and will begin proceedings. Let's play...

We are moments away from the start of the game but first, the two sets of players will line up on the field. The prime ministers will be escorted by their respective captains as they introduce their teams to their leaders. It is now time for the national anthems and it will be Australia's national anthem first followed by the national anthem of India.

Rohit Sharma the skipper of India says that they would have batted first as well but they know what they have to do now and they need to do it well. Informs they have one change with Mohammad Shami coming into the side in place of Mohammed Siraj. He adds that it is always good to have time off and it allows them an opportunity to reflect on their performance and hopefully they can get what they want in this game. Regarding the pitch, he says that the surface looks good and they are not sure when it will begin to spin but they are hoping it stays true for all five days.

Steven Smith the captain of Australia says they will be batting first and informs that there are no changes. He adds that the surface looks really good but it will be hard to say till they come out to play. Mentions that the spinners have performed well so far and they will have some help from the wicket as the game goes on. Reckons that the next series in India will be four years away which is a long time away and he would have to wait and see if he returns.

Some pre-match celebrations are underway with the prime ministers of the two nations present on the ground and are being entertained with some musical performances. We are moments away from the toss though...

Australia will be delighted by the way the team performed the last time around as they managed to outclass the hosts and pick up a vital win despite clamors of a 4-0 series whitewash loud and clear after the first two games. The captaincy of Steven Smith was spot on as he nailed every decision and impressed all with his bowling changes and tactics. They will eagerly look forward to putting in a significant performance in this match as well with their spinners in a great rhythm and the batters finally able to cope with the conditions on offer. Will they be able to claim yet another win and seal the series? Or will India come roaring back to set up a rematch at The Oval for the World Test Championship title? We will find out over the next few days. Stay tuned for the toss and team updates.

India are coming into this game on the back with a disappointing defeat in the last match where they were outplayed by the Aussies in all three departments. The host’s top-order woes continued as they collapsed in both innings without any significant contribution coming from the batters and were well behind the eight-ball right throughout the game. On the bright side, there has been ample contribution from the tail which has wagged throughout the series and has bailed the team out of tricky situations on several occasions. The Indians may look to make some changes to their batting order for this crucial game and they will hope that the lack of wickets in the fourth inning of the previous match from their world-class spinners is just a minor blip in proceedings.

Hello, and a warm welcome, ladies and gentlemen to our coverage of the fourth and final Test in the Border Gavaskar Trophy between India and Australia from the Shri Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad. The visitors have sealed a spot in the final of the ICC World Test Championship with a win in the last game and with 148 points at 68.52 PCT (%), they will clinch the top spot on the table even if they are to lose this game. India has to win this game to book their place in the finale without depending on results elsewhere. Let us see who stands tall in this fiercely contested battle between two of the cricketing giants.
